definitions.explanation: Reworking a story, play, or other creative work by changing the setting, characters, or details while preserving the basic plot or structure. Distinguished from a faithful translation or direct reproduction.

examples.japanese: シェイクスピアの{作品|さくひん}を{翻案|ほんあん}する。
この{映画|えいが}はフランスの{小説|しょうせつ}を{翻案|ほんあん}したものだ。
examples.english: This film is an adaptation of a French novel.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}には{西洋|せいよう}の{戯曲|ぎきょく}を{日本|にほん}の{設定|せってい}に{翻案|ほんあん}して{上演|じょうえん}することが{盛|さか}んに{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: During the Meiji era, Western plays were actively adapted to Japanese settings and performed.

notes:
USAGE:
{翻案|ほんあん} implies creative adaptation — changing settings, names, or cultural context — not just a direct translation. It is commonly used in literature, theater, and film criticism.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {翻案|ほんあん}{作品|さくひん} (adapted work)
- {翻案|ほんあん}{劇|げき} (adapted play)
- {原作|げんさく}を{翻案|ほんあん}する (adapt the original work)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {翻訳|ほんやく}: translation (faithful linguistic conversion)
- {改作|かいさく}: reworking, revision (broader; can mean any revision of a creative work)
- アダプテーション: adaptation (loanword, used especially in film contexts)
